actionable_steps: Treat ExoFOP as the last step, not the first: since 2026-08-19 a candidate needs a peer-reviewed paper (or an RNAAS citing previously refereed methods) plus 'Published Candidate Upload Request' approval before it can be registered; request the ExoFOP account early (affiliation field required; 'Citizen Scientist' is an accepted position) because approval is manual.

Publish the pipeline first: write a methods paper (injection-recovery, inverted-null calibration, blind recovery of known KOIs/TOIs, centroid/PRF localisation) for Astronomy & Computing (no-fee subscription route), PASP or AJ; this single paper unlocks RNAAS-then-CTOI for every later candidate.

For each surviving candidate, create a versioned Zenodo record (Preprint/Dataset, CC-BY) on day 0 with P, T0 (BJD_TDB), predicted future transits, vetting table, TRICERATOPS inputs/outputs and an environment lock; cite it in everything.

Do not submit an RNAAS on an unvalidated single candidate with unpublished methods and no professional reviewer; if you do write an RNAAS, keep it to ≤1,500 words all-in, one figure, first person singular, AASTeX 7, AI-disclosure statement at the end naming tools and tasks (AAS template), Zenodo DOI for data.

Line up one professional collaborator before any public claim: for Kepler-Bonus targets email the KBONUS authors with a data question; for TESS targets post on Planet Hunters TESS Talk and ask the PHT team about their CTOI/paper workflow; for Kepler-field candidates also contact THYME/MELANGE or NExScI (Ciardi/Furlan) for AO and stellar characterisation; one email per group, evidence pack ≤300 words plus a DOI.
If the target is TESS-detectable, file a TESS DDT (2-min cadence, ≥6 weeks before sector start, tess-ddt@mit.edu) — free, public, and it worked for Rabtsevich (DDT #100).

Use the wording ladder strictly in every public artefact (README, tweet, Zenodo title): 'transit-like signal' → 'planet candidate (unvalidated)' → 'validated planet candidate (FPP, inputs)' → 'validated planet (after refereed acceptance)' → 'confirmed (mass)'; never assign a letter; claim catalogue absence only with catalogue names and a date.

Before claiming novelty, check KOI/TCE/TOI/CTOI, NEA ps, and membership/variability catalogues (e.g. THYME/MELANGE tables) by exact Gaia ID, and ask the relevant authors which light curve they searched.

For the refereed paper, budget: AJ Tier 1 $1,425 (≤30 quanta) and ask about the AAS Publication Support Fund at submission; or MNRAS £2,356 with a discretionary RAS/OUP waiver requested at submission (not in the cover letter); after acceptance of a validated planet email exonames@ipac.caltech.edu with the acceptance letter for a Kepler/K2 number.
Get an arXiv endorser from a collaborator who has read the work; never mass-email endorsers; post the full paper rather than an RNAAS-length note to avoid the short-submission hold.

Ask Kuber for the actual AAS82222 decision letter text and for 'Steve''s identity before modelling your plan on his experience; read the X replies, r/ClaudeAI thread and Bluesky in a browser (blocked from the sandbox).
